problem_summary.summary: Convert a valid Roman numeral to its integer value, accounting for the standard subtractive pairs.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a Roman numeral string s. Return its integer value.
constraints: s contains only I, V, X, L, C, D, and M
s is valid and represents a value from 1 through 3999

brute_force.explanation: Map each symbol to its value and first add every symbol. In a second pass, subtract twice the value of each symbol that is smaller than the following symbol; its initial addition must be changed into subtraction.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Ordinary symbols contribute positively. In a valid subtractive pair, adding the smaller symbol and later subtracting twice it changes its net contribution to negative, yielding larger minus smaller.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — two passes over the string.

optimized.explanation: Scan left to right. Add a symbol's value unless its next symbol is larger, in which case subtract it. Valid Roman numerals only use the six specified subtractive pairs.
optimized.correctness_idea: A symbol before a larger symbol is exactly the smaller term in a subtractive pair and must contribute negatively. Every other symbol contributes positively, so summing these signed values implements the numeral's value.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — one pass over the string.

edge_cases.handling: Its mapped value is added directly.

edge_cases.case: Subtractive pair such as IX or CM
edge_cases.handling: The smaller symbol is subtracted and the larger one is added.
